sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for Milwaukee County property are recorded at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee, WI 53233. You can bring the paperwork to that room or mail it. The office is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the main number is (414) 278-4021.

The Register of Deeds does more than file deeds. It records, scans and indexes real estate documents, corporation papers and military discharges, records informal probate instruments, keeps financing statements, and collects the real estate transfer fee. Birth, death and marriage certificates come from the same office, so a visit for a deed and a visit for a death certificate can happen at the counter in one trip.

Milwaukee County is the most populous county in Wisconsin, with an estimated 924,216 residents on July 1, 2025 according to the Census Bureau. Every one of those residents lives inside a city or village, because Milwaukee County is the only Wisconsin county with no unincorporated towns. That means a seller never has to work out which town government sits behind the address. It is always one of 19 municipalities, 10 cities and 9 villages, and the county Register of Deeds records for all of them.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Milwaukee County?
sections.html:
Recording a standard document costs $30, no matter how many pages it has. Plats and certified copies carry separate charges, and the transfer fee is added on top when a sale is involved. The office accepts cash, checks and money orders payable to the Register of Deeds. It does not accept credit or debit cards.

Any other documents that travel with a plat are charged the standard $30 each. If the deed is a sale, the state transfer fee shows up on your transfer return receipt, and you pay it at the counter together with the recording fee.

sections.h2: How is the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee figured?
sections.html:
The fee is 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction of $100 on a conveyance that is not exempt, which works out to $3 per $1,000. Wisconsin law puts it on the grantor, the seller, and tells the register of deeds to collect it when the deed is submitted. This comes from Wis. Stat. 77.22. On a $200,000 sale the fee is $600.

Value means the full actual consideration paid or to be paid, including any lien on the property. For a gift, a nominal-price deed or a swap, the statute uses the estimated price the property would bring on the open market between a willing buyer and seller (s. 77.21). Under s. 77.24, 20 percent of what a county collects stays with the county and the rest goes to the state.

Several transfers are exempt under s. 77.25. The ones sellers and heirs run into most often are:

  • a conveyance by will, descent or survivorship;
  • a foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder or land contract seller;
  • a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments;
  • a transfer between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration;
  • a conveyance of real estate worth $1,000 or less;
  • a deed that only gives or releases security for a debt.

The register has no duty to decide whether an exemption is valid, so the reason must be stated correctly on the return. State law also bars a city, village, town or county from charging its own fee on a conveyance the state fee exempts (s. 77.256).

sections.h2: What do you need to bring or mail to record a deed in Milwaukee County?
sections.html:
You need the signed original deed, a transfer return receipt, and payment. Wisconsin law says every conveyance offered for recording must come with the return described in s. 77.22(2), and the register will not accept the deed without it. Since January 12, 2026, the Department of Revenue has taken the transfer return into its My Tax Account system, where filers do not need a username or password to file.

  • The original document or documents, completed before you submit them.
  • The transfer return receipt for any conveyance document, or the exemption reason shown on it.
  • A check payable to the Register of Deeds, or cash, for the $30 fee and any transfer fee.
  • A return name and address on the document, because the original comes back by mail.

The document itself has to meet the content rules in Wis. Stat. 706.05. It needs the signatures the law requires and must identify the land and the parties so the office can index it. A document that is to be indexed in the real estate records, modifies an original mortgage or land contract, or is a subordination agreement must carry the full legal description, and a modification must also give the document number of the original mortgage or land contract.

The register does not prepare documents, does not carry blank deed forms, and cannot say whether a document is legally sound. Owners can draft their own, hire an attorney, or ask a title company. Questions about the return itself go to the Department of Revenue, which the county page lists at (608) 266-1594 or eRETR@revenue.wi.gov.

sections.h2: How long does recording take in Milwaukee County?
sections.html:
Documents are recorded within three to five business days, in the order they are received, and the original is mailed back within one to two weeks. The office states that documents are not recorded immediately, so a closing date should leave room for this window. For questions about a pending document, email RODrecordings@milwaukeecountywi.gov or call (414) 278-4005.

For a seller, the practical point is timing around taxes and payoffs. A title company or closing attorney normally handles delivery of the deed. If you are selling to a buyer who pays cash and wants a fast close, ask the closing agent when the deed will go to the Register of Deeds and which return exemption, if any, applies to your transfer.

sections.h2: How do you remove a deceased owner from a Milwaukee County deed?
sections.html:
You record a termination of decedent's interest. For a deed that names both spouses, the county lists the Termination of Decedent's Interest form (HT-110), the transfer return with the exemption under s. 77.25(11) for a transfer by will, descent or survivorship, a copy of the recorded ownership deed, and a $30 fee. The county says it no longer requires a copy of the real estate tax bill or the death certificate.

When a transfer on death document was recorded and the owner has died, the steps are the same except the form is TOD-110 and the exemption is s. 77.25(11m). Forms and instructions are on the Wisconsin Register of Deeds Association site. This step matters to anyone selling an inherited house in Milwaukee County, because a buyer's title insurer will want the record to show who now owns the property.

To change ownership in any other way, such as adding or removing a name, a new deed has to be drafted and recorded with its transfer return. The office cannot draft it for you.

sections.h2: What is Property Fraud Alert in Milwaukee County?
sections.html:
It is a free online service that emails an owner when their exact name appears as grantor or grantee on a document recorded in the Register of Deeds office. It does not stop fraud. It gives an early warning, so an owner can act quickly if a deed or mortgage shows up that they never signed.

Sign up if you own a house you do not live in, such as a rental, an inherited property waiting for sale, or a vacant home. Names are matched exactly, so some owners register more than one spelling.

sections.h2: What is the Milwaukee County housing market like for sellers?
sections.html:
The county is mostly built up and has a large share of older homes, and the Census Bureau figures show a split between renters and owners. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied housing rate was 49.9 percent, the median value of owner-occupied homes was $230,700, and median gross rent was $1,101. The county had 392,399 households and 429,425 housing units as of July 1, 2025.

The county covers 1,189 square miles in total, but only 241 of those are land. The rest is Lake Michigan, which is why Milwaukee County has the highest density in Wisconsin at 3,890.5 people per square mile of land in 2020. The city of Milwaukee is the county seat, and the next largest places by 2020 population include West Allis, Wauwatosa, Greenfield, Oak Creek and Franklin.

These are county averages. A house in Wauwatosa, one in Oak Creek and one in the central city of Milwaukee can sit in very different tax districts and school districts, so ask the municipal treasurer for the specific tax bill before you set a price.

sections.h2: Where can Milwaukee County owners get legal help with deeds?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds cannot give legal advice, but the county page lists two places to start. The Marquette Volunteer Legal Clinic gives free, confidential and brief legal advice at House of Peace Community Center, 1702 W. Walnut Street, on Tuesdays from 4 to 6 p.m. (sign-in begins at 3:30 p.m.), phone (414) 933-1300. The Lawyer Referral and Information Service takes calls Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

For a house sale, a title company or real estate attorney will also prepare the deed and file the transfer return for you.

faqs.q: How much does the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 per document, regardless of page count, with a separate transfer fee on most sales. Plats cost $25 to $50 to record, and a condominium plat adds a $100 review fee paid by separate check. The office takes cash, checks and money orders only.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee when I sell a house in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents per $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000, set by Wis. Stat. 77.22. A $250,000 sale carries a fee of $750. The seller owes it, and it is collected when the deed is recorded. Exempt transfers, such as one by will or a foreclosure, owe nothing.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Milwaukee County without a transfer return?
faqs.a: No. Wisconsin law requires the return with every conveyance offered for recording, and the Milwaukee County office lists the receipt as required for all conveyance documents. If the transfer is exempt, the return still records the exemption reason.

faqs.q: How do I get my recorded deed back from Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: The office mails the original recorded document to the name and return address on it. Recording takes three to five business days, and the mail return takes one to two weeks. Buy a certified copy at recording if you need proof sooner.

faqs.q: Does the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds handle property tax bills?
faqs.a: No. It records documents and collects the transfer fee. Tax bills for Milwaukee County properties come from the municipality where the house sits, so ask that city or village treasurer for balances and payoffs.
